affectedPublicSurfaces: THE PRODUCTION PROMPT VERSION PIN for `optimize_product_2`. `backend/src/juli_backend/services/agent/prompts/optimize_product/` holds `v1.md`, `v2.md` and `v3.md`; this slice adds `v4.md` as a NEW FILE and moves the pin. ADR-072 d.4 makes a released version IMMUTABLE — v3's bytes must be unchanged after this diff, and runs recorded under v3 must still resolve their prompt version. Editing v3 in place would break resume for every in-flight run bound to it (`prompt_version_unrecoverable` is fail-closed by design: an unresolvable version stops the run rather than executing an unknown prompt).

THE PROPOSED-CHANGE TEXT SELLERS READ — the seller-facing half. Every completed proposal must state FOUR consequence lines: the lever (the field or the depth), the 30-day window, the ≥ 1-day price hold, and that a discount lowers the floor a future flash sale must beat. All four pass the ADR-070 outbound banned-pattern guard, in Vietnamese, second person, with no internal identifier, no projected impact magnitude and no causal claim (S-NFR-4, OP-FR-7).

THE CONFIRMATION SHAPE: exactly ONE option. `runner/confirmation.py` already mints `_SINGLE_OPTION_ID = "1"` (line 76, used at line 155) and that stays the only option id this workflow mints — N = 1, no option picker, no per-lever cap (ADR-090 d.5, S-FR-3). The prompt must not be able to produce a second option, and the assertion is on the built confirmation, not on the prompt's wording.

THE DIAGNOSIS-EVIDENCE RULE, which is the substance of v4: a field with NO returned diagnosis code is NEVER proposed. This is the rule that stops Juli asserting a verdict TikTok did not give, and it is asserted as a RELATIONSHIP — move the code from description to title and the proposed field follows.

THE ONE-LEVER RULE, restated in the prompt to match the machinery #1773 and #1778 already changed: one listing field OR one Product Discount, then the run ends. The playbook's step order and its `required_steps` are RE-STATED so the prompt and the playbook agree — the consistency gate (`tests/unit/test_agent_prompt_playbook_consistency_gate.py`) is what makes that agreement checkable rather than asserted.
THE CONFIRM-FIRST STATEMENT: this workflow is BARRED from repeat consent in v1 (ADR-090 d.6, narrowing ADR-055 d.19's `optimize_product_2` eligibility), and the shipped copy says so explicitly.

TWO BANNED CLAIMS, outright (OP-NFR-2): the Price Diagnostics TIER and the 14 card-diagnostic recommendations — no API exposes either — and 'TikTok flags…' may appear ONLY where a code was actually returned. These are enforced by the copy guard, not merely discouraged in prompt text, because a prompt instruction is exactly the thing an adversarial completion routes around.

`prompt_sha256` MOVES, so the golden scenarios re-capture ONCE. `tests/fixtures/agent_prompt_gates/` already holds `optimize_product_v1_composed.golden.md`, `_v2_`, `_v3_`; a `_v4_` golden is added and `tests/fixtures/golden_scenarios/optimize_product_confirm_pause.json` is regenerated. Both diffs are REVIEWED — a hand-edited snapshot is a green that proves nothing.

COMPOSITION, not duplication: v4 is composed through #1705's shared sections so workflow-invariant rules stay in one place and only this workflow's block changes. A rule copied into the workflow block that already lives in a shared section is a fork waiting to drift.

NO HTTP surface changes and NO schema change: nothing under `api/routes/` moves, no request or response model changes, no column is touched. Nothing under `apps/`, `packages/` or `ios/` is opened — this epic's doNotLoad list; the confirmation sheet's RENDERING of the four lines is #1787.

Mixed-version hazard, and it is the sharpest one in this lane: a run created under v3 that is SUSPENDED at CONFIRM must still resolve v3 after v4 ships. Because v4 is a new file beside an immutable v3, both versions resolve simultaneously and the pin is only what NEW runs read — that is exactly why the immutability rule exists.

migrationCompatibility.notes: NO SCHEMA CHANGE. No column, index, constraint, table or grant is touched and NO Alembic revision file is created — the executor must not open `backend/src/juli_backend/database/migrations/versions/`. `prompt_version` and `prompt_sha256` are EXISTING columns whose VALUES move; a new version string is data, never a schema object or an enum member. Stable and candidate run the identical schema and coexist on one database: v3 and v4 resolve simultaneously because v4 is a new file beside an immutable v3, so a stable process reading a v4 run row resolves v4 only if it has the file — which is why both processes must move onto the same release together, and why a v4 run must never be resumed by a stable process that lacks `v4.md`. Assert that failure mode is FAIL-CLOSED (`prompt_version_unrecoverable`), never a silent execution of a different prompt.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. Nothing about the deployed system changes: the pin stays on v3, the prompt keeps describing the OLD workflow — price vocabulary, two independent CONFIRM writes, no diagnosis — while the machinery underneath has already moved. That mismatch is a real product risk (the prompt describes a lever that no longer exists), but it is not a rollback hazard: nothing is exposed, nothing is partially applied, no vendor call is made, no data changes.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: REVERT THE PIN — a pointer move, not a delete. v4's file STAYS ON DISK, immutable, beside v3, so every run recorded under v4 still resolves its prompt version after the rollback; deleting `v4.md` would strand those runs on `prompt_version_unrecoverable` and is the one thing the revert must not do. New runs compose v3 again. Redeploy the previous release and restart `juli-api` and `juli-celery-worker` together — a stable process that lacks `v4.md` cannot resume a v4 run, and that failure is fail-closed by design (`prompt_version_unrecoverable`) rather than a silent execution of a different prompt; assert this pre-merge rather than assuming it. There is no schema to revert and no downgrade to run. The regenerated goldens revert with the code as ordinary files. A run SUSPENDED at CONFIRM across the rollback resumes correctly if and only if its own recorded version's file is present, which is precisely the guarantee immutability provides.

doNotInfer: Do NOT reintroduce BASE-PRICE VOCABULARY or a base-price write. v4 replaces price vocabulary with discount vocabulary; `update_product_price` left this workflow in #1773 and `resources.products.update_prices` has no caller on this path. A prompt that describes repricing the base price describes a tool that does not exist — and ADR-090 d.1 rejected a fallback by name.

The MODEL NEVER PICKS THE DEPTH (S-FR-4). v4 must not invite, imply or permit a model-chosen number; #1778's deterministic rule computes it and the dispatch validator refuses anything else. A prompt that asks the model to 'choose an appropriate discount' is a pricing decision made by a prompt.

Do NOT name a DEFAULT SHOP MAXIMUM or any default depth in prompt text, an example, or a golden. #1775's setting is required and seller-confirmed; a number that ships in a prompt is a number no seller ever saw.

Do NOT CLAIM A TIKTOK TIER OR A CODE THE API DID NOT RETURN (OP-NFR-2). The Price Diagnostics tier and the 14 card-diagnostic recommendations are BANNED OUTRIGHT — no API exposes them, and listing-quality tier is US-only. 'TikTok flags…' appears only where a code was actually returned. Enforce this in the copy guard, not only in prompt text: a prompt instruction is exactly what an adversarial completion routes around.

Do NOT reference SEARCH ACTIVITIES or imply a pre-proposal lock check. `POST /promotion/202309/activities/search` does not exist as a usable read (contract-collection A-25; `endpoints.md:509`); the prompt must not promise a collision check Juli cannot perform, and platform campaigns remain invisible.

Do NOT enable, imply or soften REPEAT CONSENT. Optimize Product is BARRED from it in v1 (ADR-090 d.6, narrowing ADR-055 d.19). v4 carries an explicit CONFIRM-FIRST statement; wording that suggests a future run is pre-approved contradicts the shipped eligibility rule.

Do NOT READ A MIGRATION NUMBER FROM HEAD — do not write a migration at all. This slice has no schema change. Never run `alembic heads`, never read the tip of `backend/src/juli_backend/database/migrations/versions/`, never derive a number from the newest filename. Migration numbers are RESERVED BY META.

NEVER EDIT A RELEASED PROMPT VERSION IN PLACE. v3's bytes are immutable (ADR-072 d.4). Add `v4.md`; do not 'fix a typo' in v1, v2 or v3, and do not delete an old version file — runs are bound to them.

Do NOT HAND-EDIT A GOLDEN OR A SNAPSHOT to make a gate green. Regenerate ONCE with the real runner under a clean `.venv-ci` built from `constraints.txt`, and review the diff. A local dependency drift producing a green is a known failure mode in this repo.

Do NOT put a GUARD in the prompt. The cooldown, the title-length rule and the four-field bundle refusal live in the input models and the dispatch validator (#1780); restating them in v4 as prose is fine, relying on them as prose is not.

Do NOT mint a second CONFIRMATION OPTION or introduce an option picker. `_SINGLE_OPTION_ID = "1"` stays the only option id this workflow mints (ADR-090 d.5); N > 1 needs an honest per-option comparison line that does not exist for VN and a picker that is not built.
